name: Generating language and text
gist: Papers on using diffusion and generative approaches to create text, including language models, speech synthesis, and music generation.
explain: Most generative models today use autoregressive methods for text: predict the next word, given all previous words, then repeat (like autocomplete on your phone, but more complex). Diffusion models—the 'noisy to clear' approach that dominates image generation—are less common for text, but researchers are exploring them. The question is: can we generate text using the same mathematics as images? And if we do, does it have advantages or disadvantages compared to standard methods?

One reason this is interesting is that diffusion models work differently from autoregressive ones. Autoregressive models commit to each word in sequence—once they predict 'the,' that word is fixed and influences everything that follows, so if you choose wrong early, you can't recover. Diffusion models work in parallel across all positions: they gradually refine the entire sentence at once, like sculpting stone by removing material everywhere simultaneously. This could potentially allow the model to revise earlier words if later context suggests something different (rather than getting trapped by an early wrong choice), which might lead to better outputs. It might also allow different decoding strategies—instead of being locked into 'always pick the highest-probability next word,' you could search through multiple possibilities because you're not committing irrevocably at each step.

Papers here explore whether diffusion works for language at all (since most text uses autoregressive methods, diffusion is a natural next experiment), whether it's competitive with autoregressive methods, and whether the different generation process enables new capabilities (like better revision or more diverse outputs). The research is still early—text diffusion does not yet beat standard methods for most tasks—but the work here is mapping out what is possible. Some papers apply image-generation techniques (like flow matching) to text, which is interesting because it might give text generation new properties image generation enjoys (like multi-scale refinement or better diversity). Others use diffusion for specific text tasks like paraphrase (rewriting sentences differently) where having a different generation process might help because you can revise multiple parts of a sentence in parallel rather than being forced into a linear left-to-right path. And some work on combined problems: generating both image and text descriptions together, which requires bridging the gap between two very different types of data.

papers.title: Data Provenance for Image Auto-Regressive Generation
papers.contribution: The approach enables robust detection of IAR-generated images across a wide range of autoregressive models without watermarking.

papers.title: GoR: A Unified and Extensible Generative Framework for Ordinal Regression
papers.contribution: Theoretically establishes bias-variance error bound and proposes Coverage-Distinctiveness Index metric; extensive experiments on 17 ordinal regression benchmarks show effectiveness.

papers.title: Latent Denoising Makes Good Tokenizers
papers.contribution: LDT consistently improves generation quality across six representative generative models on class-conditioned ImageNet and text-conditioned MSCOCO benchmarks compared to prior tokenizers.

papers.title: Logit‑KL Flow Matching: Non‑Autoregressive Text Generation via Sampling‑Hybrid Inference
papers.contribution: Improves perplexity and downstream metrics over NAR baselines for unconditional and conditional text and code infilling.

papers.title: MUSE: Resolving Manifold Misalignment in Visual Tokenization via Topological Orthogonality
papers.contribution: Breaks the reconstruction-abstraction tradeoff, achieving state-of-the-art generation (gFID 3.08) while outperforming teacher model InternViT-300M in linear probing (85.2% vs 82.5%).

papers.title: Speculative Coupled Decoding for Training-Free Lossless Acceleration of Autoregressive Visual Generation
papers.contribution: Achieves up to 4.2× speedup in image generation and 13.6× in video generation without quality degradation or draft model training.

papers.title: VideoFlexTok: Flexible-Length Coarse-to-Fine Video Tokenization
papers.contribution: Achieves comparable generation quality with 5x smaller model (1.1B vs 5.2B) and enables 10-second 81-frame videos with 8x fewer tokens than 3D grid tokenizers.

papers.title: reAR: Rethinking Visual Autoregressive Models via Token-wise Consistency Regularization
papers.contribution: reAR reduces ImageNet gFID from 3.02 to 1.86 and achieves gFID 1.42 with 177M parameters, matching larger diffusion models; with advanced tokenizers achieves IS of 316.9.

papers.title: (1D) Ordered Tokens Enable Efficient Test-Time Search
papers.contribution: Shows AR models with coarse-to-fine ordered tokens exhibit improved test-time scaling and enables training-free text-to-image generation using pure search over sequences.

papers.title: AC-Foley: Reference-Audio-Guided Video-to-Audio Synthesis with Acoustic Transfer
papers.contribution: AC-Foley achieves fine-grained Foley generation with state-of-the-art performance, enabling zero-shot generation of sounds and timbre transfer without training on specific datasets.

papers.title: Autoregressive Image Generation with Masked Bit Modeling
papers.contribution: Achieves state-of-the-art gFID of 0.99 on ImageNet-256, significantly reducing sampling costs and converging faster than continuous approaches.

papers.title: BEAT: Tokenizing and Generating Symbolic Music by Uniform Temporal Steps
papers.contribution: Improved musical quality and structural coherence compared to event-based methods with higher efficiency and more effective capture of long-range patterns in music continuation and accompaniment generation tasks.

papers.title: Concept-Guided Tokenization: Closing the Gap Between Reconstruction and Generation
papers.contribution: Achieves rFID of 1.39 on ImageNet reconstruction, gFID of 2.65 on class-conditional generation, and 10.73 on text-to-image generation, bridging reconstruction-generation divide.

papers.title: Declarative Audio Editing with Audio Language Model
papers.contribution: SmartDJ achieves superior perceptual quality, spatial realism, and semantic alignment for declarative stereo audio editing compared to prior methods.

papers.title: FS-DFM: Fast and Accurate Long Text Generation with Few-Step Diffusion Language Models
papers.contribution: Achieves 1024-token generation with 8 sampling steps at perplexity parity to 1024-step baselines, delivering 128× faster sampling.

papers.title: GarmentGPT: Compositional Garment Pattern Generation via Discrete Latent Tokenization
papers.contribution: First framework for latent space generation of sewing patterns achieving 95.62% panel accuracy and 81.84% stitch accuracy on structured datasets, significantly outperforming existing methods.

papers.title: Hyperspherical Latents Improve Continuous-Token Autoregressive Generation
papers.contribution: Achieves FID 1.34 on ImageNet for AR models; at smaller scales surpasses larger baselines like MAR and VAR.

papers.title: SSG: Scaled Spatial Guidance for Multi-Scale Visual Autoregressive Generation
papers.contribution: SSG achieves consistent gains in fidelity and diversity across VAR models while preserving low latency, revealing untapped efficiency in coarse-to-fine generation.

papers.title: SyncTrack: Rhythmic Stability and Synchronization in Multi-Track Music Generation
papers.contribution: Significantly improves multi-track music quality through enhanced rhythmic consistency, measured by novel metrics (IRS, CBS, CBD).

papers.title: Topology-Preserved Auto-regressive Mesh Generation in the Manner of Weaving Silk
papers.contribution: Ensures critical properties (manifoldness, watertightness, face normal consistency, part awareness) and achieves state-of-the-art compression efficiency with intricate mesh generation.

papers.title: ViTok-v2: Scaling Native Resolution Autoencoders to 5 Billion Parameters
papers.contribution: Matches state-of-the-art reconstruction at 256p and outperforms across benchmarks at 512p and higher resolutions while maintaining flexibility for arbitrary aspect ratios.

papers.title: Visual Implicit Autoregressive Modeling
papers.contribution: Achieves FID 2.16 on ImageNet 256x256 with 38.4% parameters of VAR, enabling reduction from 19.24GB to 8.53GB peak memory and doubling throughput.

papers.title: WeTok: Powerful Discrete Tokenization for High-Fidelity Visual Reconstruction
papers.contribution: WeTok achieves record-low zero-shot rFID of 0.12 at high-fidelity setting on ImageNet 50k, outperforming FLUX-VAE and SD-VAE 3.5, and zero-shot rFID of 3.49 at 768x compression ratio.

papers.title: YuE: Scaling Open Foundation Models for Long-Form Music Generation
papers.contribution: YuE scales to trillions of tokens generating up to five minutes of music, matching or exceeding proprietary systems in musicality and vocal agility as of January 2025.

papers.title: mCLM: A Modular Chemical Language Model that Generates Functional and Makeable Molecules
papers.contribution: mCLM with 3B parameters significantly improves chemical functions critical for drug development and synthetic accessibility compared to 7 other leading generative AI methods including GPT-5.
